assessment:
Three opponents have decided you are the friendly seat. They are right about the cards and completely wrong about the reason. Every wish here is a delivery rather than an arrival — Enlightened Tutor and Mystical Tutor put the card on top, Long-Term Plans buries it third — and the couriers are the draw engines you handed out yourself. Your generosity IS the delivery system, so count your draws per turn before you name a card. Every time.

Two clocks give these three cards their jobs. The verified storm kill (stack 006) wants its fourth piece scheduled and never shown: Enlightened Tutor reaches every artifact piece of it at instant speed, and Long-Term Plans is the only card in the 99 that can find its one creature. The clean kill (stack 002) wants Approach of the Second Sun on top, and Mystical Tutor is that line's own verified setup.

Then spend them like access, because half the time they ARE the access. You reach a win condition by turn six in 50.5% of games — in the other half these three cards are the whole route there, so stop playing them as card selection and start playing them as the win.

targets.scenario: Turn 1 or 2, {W} open at an opponent's end step. Your hand has lands and engines but no card advantage, and the pod has not sorted its threats yet.
targets.why: Take the default wish and spend the tell on a card that is not the kill. Study on top, drawn, cast on turn 2 is a firehose in a pod this dense with forced action — every opponent spell becomes a card or a tax, and the long game is decided in exactly that currency. An early Enlightened Tutor reads as value, which is precisely the information schedule you want to be running.

targets.scenario: You are at 26 and falling. The aggro seat has connected twice and you are currently the cheapest attack at the table.
targets.why: Go and get the wall, and understand you are fetching combo protection rather than defence. Stack 006's fifteen-cast minimum is computed from 32 life, and the requirement scales the wrong way as you fall: 20 life makes it sixteen casts, 8 life makes it seventeen, and every extra cast is another priority window you hand three opponents. Charge two per attacker and protect the ledger.

targets.scenario: Hullbreaker Horror and both rocks are accounted for — on the battlefield or in hand behind counter mana. The Reservoir is the only missing piece, and it is the end step of the opponent to your right.
targets.why: Fire the signature wish at their end step and let your draw step deliver the confession. The commit turn then opens with Grand Abolisher, having never shown the table a three-of-four board — and stack 006 does the rest: fifteen casts from 32 life, three fifty-point activations, dead table. The loudest card in the deck should spend zero turns on the battlefield before the turn it wins.

targets.scenario: Midgame. You hold Hullbreaker Horror and Sol Ring, the second rock is missing, and your hand is bulging past seven off your own engines.
targets.why: Fetch the kill piece wearing a utility card's face. Stack 004 pins the loop to Hullbreaker plus Sol Ring plus any two-mana rock, and Thought Vessel qualifies exactly — while the no-maximum-hand-size clause gives you a cover story that happens to be true. It hoards your doubled draws and survives the creature wraths The Second Doctor does not.

tutors.notes: The reveal is public and the timing does the talking. Cast it early and the table files it as value. Cast it late at an end step and every awake opponent reads 'the go turn is their untap' — so run that version behind untapped counter mana, or on a board that does not already look like three of four.

targets.scenario: Rocks and Reservoir are accounted for and the Horror is the missing piece. Font of Mythos or a doubled Howling Mine has you drawing three or more per turn.
targets.why: Grant the wish only this card can grant. Enlightened Tutor stops at artifacts and enchantments and Mystical Tutor at instants and sorceries, so Plans is the kill's one creature's only courier in the 99. Buried third under a Font it is in hand on your next draw step, and stacks 004 and 006 take it from there — so cast Plans on the turn your draw count makes 'third' mean 'tomorrow'.

targets.scenario: The first Approach of the Second Sun resolved turns ago, Mystical Tutor is spent or absent, and your engines are drawing you three cards a turn.
targets.why: Take the backup route to the stack 002 win. Third from the top is far shallower than the seventh its own first cast bought, and at three draws a turn the winning second cast is one draw step out. The only window anyone gets is while it sits on the stack, so hold the counter mana that walk budgeted before you commit.

targets.scenario: You flipped Heliod early, the table has named you the problem, and two seats are sitting on what smells like mass removal.
targets.why: Put the panic button on a schedule while you still have the schedule. Your engines make third-from-the-top a one-turn wait, and once Protection is in hand every wrath and every alpha strike at your seat is a bluff you have already called. Being the archenemy is entirely comfortable when the table cannot actually kill you.

targets.scenario: Your commit turn is two draws out, the kill pieces are gathering, and the table has started counting your artifacts.
targets.why: Fetch the shield in secret, because Plans is the one tutor here that reveals nothing. He arrives on schedule, gets cast as the commit turn's first spell, and closes every priority window stack 006 honestly opens — no opponent spells, no artifact, creature or enchantment activations, all turn. The table read your Plans as card selection.

tutors.notes: Third from the top is a schedule, not a sentence, so count your draws per turn before you cast it. On a bare board the wish is three draw steps away; under Howling Mine two; under Font of Mythos, or a Mine doubled by Alhammarret's Archive or Teferi's Ageless Insight, your very next draw step. Advance the schedule with Temple Bell, Mikokoro or Folio of Fancies when the turn demands it.

targets.scenario: The first Approach resolved — 7 life banked, the card buried seventh. It is the end step before your turn and you hold {U} for the tutor plus counter backup for tomorrow.
targets.why: Do the thing this card exists to do, and do it at their end step. Stack 002 walks the exact line, counter war included: tutor, draw it, cast it, and the win is checked while it resolves — the first casting still counts. You can only be stopped while the second Approach sits on the stack, so bring the Swan Song that walk budgeted and cast nothing else that turn.

targets.scenario: Two seats have flooded the board, your walkers are taking chip attacks, and the control player is holding up counter mana like a toll booth.
targets.why: Fetch the wrath that cannot be countered and swing at it through their open mana — that open mana is the reason this is the fetch. Your clock lives in artifacts and enchantments, and the sim has you at 1.513 bodies by turn six, so sweep freely: you are trading their board for almost nothing of yours, and all four walkers live through it in both directions.

targets.scenario: The commit turn is scheduled for your untap, kill pieces in hand, and you want insurance more than you want another threat.
targets.why: Buy the last word instead of another threat. The commit turn's one interactable moment is the response window to Grand Abolisher himself, and a Veto that cannot be countered closes it on your terms. Fetch it the end step before, while the table is still reading your Mystical Tutor as digging for action.

tutors.notes: The reveal is public here too, and an end-step Mystical Tutor after a first Approach is read correctly by anyone awake. Cast it at the last legal moment and price the counter war in before you tap, not after.

gaps: No tutor in this deck puts a card into your hand — every wish is a delivery, top or top or third, and a delivery can die in transit to a well-timed answer. The engines are the couriers, so count your per-turn draws before you count on the fetch.

The kill's one creature has exactly one courier: only Long-Term Plans can find Hullbreaker Horror, and only Plans or Mystical Tutor can find Approach of the Second Sun. Lose the courier a line depends on and that line runs on raw draws — so hold Plans for the piece nothing else reaches, not for the piece you happen to want.

Two of the three wishes are announced. Treat the reveal, not the mana, as these cards' real price and budget it like the information it is: keep Long-Term Plans for the secrets and let the other two carry the cover story.
